tasks.short: Plan the week's programme of instruction, demonstration and work time, set up materials and corners, lead circle time, guide work time, and share the week plan with the duo teacher.

steps.what: Kindergarten teacher plans a balanced program of instruction, demonstration and work time for the week
Kindergarten teacher sets up materials and classroom corners
Kindergarten teacher conducts instruction and demonstration in circle time
Kindergarten teacher guides work time where children observe, question and investigate
Kindergarten teacher e-mails the week plan to the duo teacher

tasks.design: Week plans use a template in the school's document space ({DOCS}) linked to the theme and the development lines, starting from last year's plan for the same theme. Once the teacher has finished the plan, it is shared with the duo teacher on the same page instead of by e-mail. Setting up the classroom, circle time and guiding work time stay with the teacher.
tasks.previous_blocker: Week plans were written fresh and e-mailed to the duo teacher.
tasks.enabler_now: Shared planning templates in document spaces are common in schools.
tasks.still_hard: The week rarely goes as planned with young children.
tasks.human_edge: Following a child's question into an unplanned investigation.

reach.learn: Whether shared plans cut handover questions.

evidence.claim: Shared document spaces can hold planning templates linked to themes.

assumptions: Boundary: from the theme plan to the plan shared; the school's yearly curriculum is outside.
Input contract: themes and development lines set by the kindergarten team; fallback is writing fresh plans.
Circle time and work time do not change.
The duo teacher's time does not change.
research_questions: Do teachers reuse last year's week plans?

incremental.description: Kindergarten teacher notes what worked in the plan for next year.

approvals.approved_version: The week plan as finished by the teacher in s1.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: new themes without earlier plans; high: repeat themes with last year's plans.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Gather notes on the child, propose meeting times, have parents choose a time, meet the parents, consult colleagues, the support coordinator and the head, and record the agreements.

steps.what: Kindergarten teacher gathers observations and notes on the child before the meeting
Kindergarten teacher proposes meeting times to parents by e-mail and phone
Parents reply with a time that suits them
Kindergarten teacher confers with parents to resolve the child's behavioral or academic problems
Kindergarten teacher confers with other teachers, counselors and administrators
Kindergarten teacher writes the agreements in the pupil record

tasks.design: The pupil record ({OTHER}) shows a child's observation tags, notes and earlier agreements on one page before the meeting. Parents pick a meeting slot in the school's parent app instead of e-mailing back and forth. Agreements go into a short template in the record. Meeting parents and conferring with colleagues, the support coordinator and the head stay with the teacher.
tasks.previous_blocker: Notes were gathered from several places and meeting times arranged by e-mail and phone.
tasks.enabler_now: School parent apps offer slot booking; pupil records show notes on one page.
tasks.still_hard: Hard conversations with parents need time to prepare in person.
tasks.human_edge: Helping worried parents and the school agree on one approach.

reach.learn: Whether parents book slots in the app.

evidence.claim: ParnasSys holds pupil records and includes the Parro parent app.
Under the WMS, parents consent to rules on pupil data.

assumptions: Boundary: from the child's concern to the recorded agreements; formal support plans are outside.
Input contract: notes in the pupil record; slots opened by the teacher; fallback is e-mail and phone.
Parents pick a slot in the app in about the time they took to reply by e-mail; priced as customer time.
Meetings with parents and colleagues do not change.

incremental.description: Kindergarten teacher opens meeting slots in the parent app.
Parents pick a meeting slot in the parent app.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: few meetings and parents who prefer phone; high: many meetings and parents on the app.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Choose and plan games, crafts, music and stories, prepare materials, lead the activities, request craft supplies from the school office, and tidy up.

steps.what: Kindergarten teacher chooses and plans games, arts and crafts, music and storytelling
Kindergarten teacher prepares materials for the activities
Kindergarten teacher organizes and leads activities to promote physical, mental and social development
Kindergarten teacher e-mails the school office for craft supplies
Kindergarten teacher tidies and stores materials

tasks.design: Songs, recordings, stories and craft ideas per theme sit in the school's media library ({DOCS}) with material lists, so planning starts from what the team already uses. Once the teacher has planned, the material list goes to the school office as a request in the purchasing form ({PROCUREMENT}). Preparing, leading activities and tidying stay with the teacher.
tasks.previous_blocker: Activities were planned from memory and supplies requested by e-mail.
tasks.enabler_now: School media libraries hold songs and recordings; request forms route to the office.
tasks.still_hard: The best activity depends on the group's energy that day.
tasks.human_edge: Getting the whole class singing and moving together.

evidence.claim: School media libraries can hold songs, recordings and activity ideas per theme.

assumptions: Boundary: from the theme plan to materials stored; the school's purchasing is outside.
Input contract: media library kept by the kindergarten team; fallback is planning from memory.
research_questions: Does the media library get used?

incremental.description: Kindergarten teacher adds new songs and ideas to the library.

approvals.approved_version: The material list in the activity plan as finished by the teacher in s1.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: a teacher with a well-known repertoire; high: a newer teacher building a repertoire.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Prepare the progress talk from the development record, propose talk times, have parents choose a time, meet parents to discuss progress, priorities and resource needs, record agreements, and pass needs to the support coordinator.

steps.what: Kindergarten teacher prepares the progress talk from the development record
Kindergarten teacher proposes talk times to parents on paper lists and by e-mail
Parents choose a talk time
Kindergarten teacher meets parents to discuss their children's progress and to determine their priorities and resource needs
Kindergarten teacher writes the agreed priorities and needs in the pupil record
Kindergarten teacher passes resource needs to the support coordinator

tasks.design: The development record ({OTHER}) prints a one-page progress overview per child with the development lines and recent notes, so the teacher does not compile it. Parents choose talk slots in the school's parent app instead of on paper lists at the door. Agreed priorities go into a short template in the record. The talk with parents and passing needs to the support coordinator stay with the teacher.
tasks.previous_blocker: Overviews were compiled by hand and talk times arranged on paper lists.
tasks.enabler_now: Pupil records print progress overviews; parent apps offer slot booking.
tasks.still_hard: Parents' priorities for their child can differ from the school's.
tasks.human_edge: Hearing what parents worry about but do not say.

reach.task: Plan a talk about their child

evidence.claim: ParnasSys holds pupil records with learning-goal tracking and includes the Parro parent app.
Under the WMS, parents consent to rules on pupil data.

assumptions: Boundary: from the development record to needs passed on; arranging extra support is outside.
Input contract: development records kept by the teacher; slots opened in the parent app; fallback is paper lists.
Parents choose a slot in the app in about the time they took on the paper list; priced as customer time.
The talk with parents does not change.

incremental.description: Kindergarten teacher opens talk slots in the parent app.
Parents choose a talk slot in the parent app.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: a small class and parents who prefer paper; high: a large class with most parents on the app.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The kindergarten teacher keeps planning with care, leading activities and meeting parents; e-mailing plans, gathering notes and arranging times by hand shrink.
skills_to_grow: Using the parent app for appointments
role.ambitious_version: A teacher with more time for each child and family.
